# selfdoc check

Check documentation coverage, directive resolution, and lint rules, each lint at the value its option in .strictmetadata/options/docs.toml sets (off: not reported; warn: reported, never blocking; error: as registered) -- and write: it advances the content and description baseline of every page it does not report stale or drifted in .strictmetadata/.docs-state/hashes/hashes.json and commits the store, which is why check is a mutating command and not a read-only one

**Effect:** mutating

## Flags

| Name | Short | Type | Presence | Env | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `--auto-commit`, `--no-auto-commit` |  | bool | optional |  | Automatically commit .strictmetadata/.docs-state/hashes/hashes.json, the staleness baseline store this run advanced, after checking. Omitted, it commits; pass --no-auto-commit to leave the store written but uncommitted -- the store is written either way |
| `--version-override` |  | str | optional |  | Project version that version-bearing generated content is expected to embed (version-mismatch-in-generated-root-file), instead of the version currently recorded in the project manifest (VERSION, pyproject.toml or package.json). Pass the same value given to 'selfdoc gen --version-override' so the check runs correctly in the release window between generation and the version bump |
